examples/local-quickstart/main.go.description: Go CRUD quickstart: create, read, update and delete one note on DynamoDB Local.

examples/cdk-multilang/local/run-local.s.description: Cross-language no-drift check with encryption: Go writes one item whose secret is encrypted through the local KMS, then TypeScript and Python read the same item and decrypt the secret, and the generated CDK construct is drift-checked. Gap: the KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants); the envelope cryptography and KMS calls are real.

examples/cdk-multilang/local/go/writer.g.description: Go writer half of the cross-language no-drift check: writes the shared item with a KMS-encrypted secret and asserts it decrypts on read; executed inside run-local.sh. Gap: the KMS is emulated.

examples/cdk-multilang/local/read.mts.description: Node.js reader half of the cross-language no-drift check; decrypts the KMS-encrypted secret through the local KMS; executed inside run-local.sh.

examples/cdk-multilang/local/read.py.description: Python reader half of the cross-language no-drift check; decrypts the KMS-encrypted secret through the local KMS; executed inside run-local.sh.

examples/multi-tenant/cmd/local/main.go.description: Multi-tenant API as a real HTTP server: health, JWT authorizer refusals, organization creation and authenticated reads with real tenant-isolation responses.

examples/multi-tenant/cmd/lambda/main.go.description: Lambda adapter driven through its route-matrix tests: API Gateway proxy events, loopback HTTP through the shared router, and the warm API-key authorizer.

examples/multi-tenant/cmd/token/main.go.description: Token CLI: mints the HS256 bearer token the local server verifies, and refuses incomplete arguments.

ts/examples/local.ts.description: TypeScript runtime CRUD example: table creation, conditional create, query paging, update and delete.

py/examples/local_crud.py.description: Python runtime CRUD example: table creation, put, get and a sort-key begins_with query.

examples/basic/contacts/main.go.description: Contacts CLI driven through its checked-in stdin transcript: create, list, gsi-email, gsi-phone, gsi-name, favorite, delete, with output assertions.

examples/basic/notes/main.go.description: Notes CLI driven through its checked-in stdin transcript: create, list, gsi-user, gsi-category, recent, stats, with output assertions.

examples/basic/todo/main.go.description: Todo CLI driven through its checked-in stdin transcript: create, list, complete and delete, with output assertions.

examples/initialization/main.go.description: Local initialization mode creates the table and performs a real TableTheory write/read on DynamoDB Local. The aws, profile, minimal and debug modes resolve real AWS defaults; they are the named cloud gap and never run in the harness.

examples/optimization/main.go.description: Library demo: the query planner runs locally without DynamoDB, and the same runner executes the examples/testing mock-based unit-test suite. Fakes here are test doubles for unit tests, not example verification.

examples/testing/user_service_test.go.description: Mock-based unit-test suite demonstrating pkg/mocks; executed by the library-demo runner. It runs locally without DynamoDB by design.

examples/release-state/main.go.description: Real TransactWrite on DynamoDB Local: actual-state update, event append and conditional outbox create, read-back assertions, plus refusal of a stale expected version.

examples/typed-go/main.go.description: Typed generic API driver: table creation, typed create/get/update and a begins_with query on DynamoDB Local, with read-back assertions.

examples/drivers/main.go.description: Driver for the loose examples/*.go snippets: seeds each table, runs the real snippet functions and asserts the conditional, transaction, batch-get, list-operation, embedded-struct and FaceTheory TTL outcomes.

examples/feature_spotlight.go.description: Conditional helpers, transaction builder and batch-get builder snippets; executed inside examples/drivers.

examples/list_operations_example.go.description: List and set update snippets; executed inside examples/drivers.

examples/embedded_structs_example.go.description: Embedded-struct single-table snippets; executed inside examples/drivers.

examples/facetheory_ttl_cache_example.go.description: FaceTheory ISR cache metadata shape and freshness helpers; executed inside examples/drivers.

ts/examples/release-state.ts.description: TypeScript release-state driver: the same real TransactWrite, read-back and stale-version refusal as the Go and Python rows, with an identical parity line.

py/examples/gsi_query.py.description: Python GSI query on DynamoDB Local: creates the table and index, writes two users and asserts the email index returns only the matching row.

py/examples/release_state.py.description: Python release-state driver: the same real TransactWrite, read-back and stale-version refusal as the Go and TypeScript rows, with an identical parity line.

examples/encryption/main.go.description: KMS envelope round-trip through TableTheory on DynamoDB Local and the local KMS emulator: the plaintext field round-trips on read, and a raw GetItem proves the stored attribute is a v2 envelope whose ciphertext does not contain the plaintext. Gap: the KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants); the envelope cryptography and KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls are real.

examples/lambda/main.go.description: Lambda handler example; T4a runs it through the Lambda runtime interface with real event payloads.

examples/payment/lambda/process/handler..description: Payment processing handler; T4a provisions tables and invokes it through API Gateway events.

examples/payment/lambda/query/handler.go.description: Payment query handler; T4a invokes it through API Gateway events.

examples/payment/lambda/reconcile/handle.description: Payment reconcile handler; T4a runs it with generated S3 events on the T3 emulator.

ts/examples/lambda/handler.ts.description: TypeScript Lambda handler; T4a runs it as a real handler through the runtime interface.

py/examples/lambda_stream_handler.py.description: Python stream handler; T4a feeds it stream events generated from real local writes (L3: managed stream delivery).

examples/blog/authorizer/main.go.description: Blog authorizer Lambda; T4b runs the real authorizer locally with the identity-bypass flag unset.

examples/blog/cmd/comments/main.go.description: Blog comments Lambda; T4b runs it through the runtime interface against local models.

examples/blog/cmd/posts/main.go.description: Blog posts Lambda; T4b runs it through the runtime interface against local models.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/go/main.g.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Go handler; T4b runs it locally with the T3 KMS/S3 emulators.

examples/cdk-multilang/bin/app.ts.description: CDK app entrypoint; T4b synthesizes it as the infrastructure-only row for this example and asserts the stack shape.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/node/hand.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Node handler; T4b runs the real handler locally with the T3 KMS/S3 emulators.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/archive/h.description: Deployed cdk-multilang archive handler; T4b drives it with generated archive events against local backends.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/python/ha.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Python handler; T4b runs the real handler locally with the T3 KMS/S3 emulators.

examples/cdk-multilang/scripts/smoke.sh.description: Deployed-AWS smoke script: it requires a deployed stack and real credentials, so T4b owns its local replacement.

examples/multi-tenant.description: The example's separate Go module: go test ./... across auth, handlers, cmd and the DynamoDB Local tests package. Handler unit tests use the in-process fake; real-DynamoDB coverage comes from the route-matrix and HTTP rows.
